title: introduce-targeted-presubmit-slimline-and-dep-pruner-operator
author: Maya Brennan
description: Motivation: our presubmit CI has grown noisy and slow due to monolithic lint/test lanes that run across the entire monorepo for non-impactful changes. At the same time, transitive dev-dependencies and stale tooling in package manifests cause intermittent CI cache churn and unnecessary build costs. This PR implements two complementary improvements: (1) a targeted presubmit strategy that runs only lightweight checks and narrowly scoped lint/test shards based on path-aware change detection, and (2) a new dep-pruner operator (action + small CLI) that detects and suggests removal of unused dev-deps and flags version instabilities. The intent is to preserve strong correctness guarantees while giving fast feedback for small changes and surfacing dependency debt for maintainers to triage. Highlights/what changed: - Introduce .github/actions/dep-pruner (composite action) and a minimal Go CLI (tools/dep-pruner) that computes unused dev-deps across package.json / pyproject.toml roots. The action runs in a dry-run by default and posts PR comments with suggested edits. - Add path-aware presubmit runner: .github/workflows/presubmit-slimline.yml. The workflow contains three lanes: quick (fast lint + unit smoke), targeted (pattern-driven test shards), and full (fallback that runs full integration on release branches). Quick runs on push for small changes; targeted is triggered when changed files exceed patterns for a module. - Move heavy lint rules behind a staged lint gate; add 'lint-shadow' job that only runs full lint when more than N files touched or explicit label is set. - Add a lightweight test selector script (scripts/select-tests-by-diff.py) that maps changed files to Jest/Pytest shards via a simple config under ci/test-mapping.yaml. - Introduce dep-stability-probe: a periodic job (weekly) that detects transitive version drift and files an issue with a report. - Add infra docs: docs/ci/presubmit-strategy.md and docs/ci/dep-pruner.md. Checklist: - [x] design doc and implementation for presubmit lanes - [x] composite action + CLI with unit tests - [x] workflow templates and mapping file - [x] docs and contributor guide updates - [x] initial integration tests against a lightweight staging runner - [x] staged rollout plan (canary on selected repos) Rollout plan: 1) Deploy workflows in dry-run mode for 48 hours to gather metrics (CI time, jobs avoided). 2) Enable auto PR comments from dep-pruner for contributors with opt-in flag. 3) After one week of metrics, enable lint-shadow gate for all repos. Backwards compatibility and safety: - Presubmit workflows default to conservative thresholds; full workflow is still the default for release/* branches. - dep-pruner never mutates files automatically; suggestions are comments and draft PRs behind a toggled flag. Related tickets: ENG-7721 (presubmit redesign), ENG-7818 (dep hygiene initiative), SUP-501 (customer-incurred CI cost spike).
commit_summaries: feat(ci): add presubmit-slimline workflow and test selector script
feat(actions): new composite dep-pruner action and Go CLI (dry-run only)
refactor(ci): stage lint into quick/targeted/full lanes with lint-shadow job
docs(ci): add presubmit strategy and dep-pruner operational docs
test(ci): add unit tests for dep-pruner and integration smoke for targeted lane
review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice approach. Can we ensure the test-mapping file is maintained by module owners? Otherwise we risk drift.
Maya Brennan: Added a maintenance note in docs/ci/presubmit-strategy.md and an owner field in ci/test-mapping.yaml.
Sofia Ramirez: dep-pruner output looks good, but please make the CLI less chatty by default (added --quiet).
Anand Gupta: Please add a feature flag so repo admins can opt into automatic draft-PR creation later.
Maya Brennan: Implemented feature flag as INPUT_CREATE_DRAFT_PR for composite action; default off.
release_notes: Introduce targeted presubmit lanes to reduce CI feedback time and add a dep-pruner operator that surfaces unused dev-dependencies and version instability; no automatic file changes by default.
notes_for_reviewers: This PR touches CI entrypoints and a small internal tool; keep an eye on cache key semantics in workflows. If you maintain any test mapping, please verify mappings in ci/test-mapping.yaml. The dep-pruner is intentionally conservative; real removals are manual until we prove stability.
